request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Holds now have a from-date and an optional to-date, and a person can have several. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it works now**
- **Storage:** a new migration (`V26__person_hold.sql`) adds a `person_hold` table with one row per hold. It drops the old `person.held` column. Anyone who was on hold before keeps an open-ended hold dating from the beginning of time.
- **Totals:** a claim is left out of the live totals only if all three are true: it is open (OPEN or PENDING), it is dated within one of the person's holds (both ends included), and no statement has bound it. Settled claims and statement-bound claims always count. The server (`Person.countsLive`) and the screen (`liveClaims`) apply the same rule, so the person's figures, the sheet totals, period totals, statements and the audit's ROLLUP/TOTALS lines all agree.
- **Hold action:** the same endpoint now adds a hold instead of switching it on and off. A blank from-date means the sheet's today and a blank to-date means no end. The audit line is `PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>`. There is no release action and no `PERSON_RELEASED` record any more.
- **Screen:** each person's row still shows `person-hold` (yes if they have any hold). It also lists each hold (`person-hold-line`) and has two date fields (`person-hold-from`, `person-hold-to`). The existing `person-hold-toggle` button, now labelled "Hold", adds the hold.

**Decisions you may want to check**
- **Refusals:** a date that isn't a real date, or a to-date before the from-date, is refused. Nothing is stored or audited, and `person-error` is shown. The request didn't say this, and the test doesn't cover it.
- **Pending claims:** I counted a claim as "bound by a statement" if a statement bound it at all, even while it is PENDING. So a PENDING claim that a statement bound stays in the totals even if it falls inside a hold. If you meant only claims whose bound figure is in use (which excludes PENDING), it is a one-line change in each place.

I also updated the comments that described the old yes/no hold.
